speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Speaker, Sir, with your permission, may I take Question Nos 15 and 16 together?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Within our public healthcare institutions where reprocessing and sterilisation of instruments are conducted, there are standard operating procedures in place to ensure that these processes are completed properly.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: There are at least three layers of checks.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: First, the mechanical parameters of the sterilisation machinery, such as temperature, pressure and time, are recorded.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Staff operating the machines would check the parameters after each cycle of sterilisation to ensure that the parameters are correct to achieve effective sterilisation.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Second, a chemical indicator affixed outside the pack of instruments to be sterilised would reflect a colour change to verify that sterilisation was complete and effective.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Only then should the staff in charge of sterilisation release the instruments for storage and use.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Third, end-users should ensure that the instrument has been sterilised before use by verifying the change in colour of the chemical indicator as well as checking the integrity of the packaging.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Staff who perform sterilisation processes would have to undergo proper training.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In our public healthcare institutions, such training is a basic requirement of a new staff’s orientation programme.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Competency assessments are also being conducted before staff are deemed competent for the function.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In addition, staff are regularly sent for further training and re-assessments in order to maintain their competencies.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The public healthcare institutions also conduct routine internal audits on various critical functions, such as the sterilisation process and workflow.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Depending on the institution’s internal work processes, such internal audits may take place as often as once every six months, involving various departments, such as Infection Control and/or Quality Assurance.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The audit findings are typically shared at learning platforms, where improvements and recommendations will be made system-wide.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: NHG’s investigations showed that the incident was a result of human error, with a lapse in adherence to the established sterilisation process and verification protocol.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: On 28 November 2018, a staff from TTSH Dental Clinic loaded instruments, which have undergone manual cleaning and disinfection in an ultrasonic washer, into the autoclave machine for the final stage of steam sterilisation.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: However, the staff did not initiate the steam sterilisation cycle.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Subsequently, the packs were unloaded and stored without realising that the packs had not undergone the final step of sterilisation.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: These packs were not verified for sterility before use.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: After the instruments were recalled, eight packs were unaccounted for and could have been used on patients.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: NHG's investigations also revealed supervisory lapses in the sterilisation workflows and escalation of the incident.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Following the incident, TTSH has reinforced safety controls across the hospital to improve vigilance and adherence to processes, so as to prevent any recurrence.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Specifically, safety controls for the TTSH Dental Clinic have been fortified in the following key areas.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Specifically, the steps of loading the autoclave machine and starting of the sterilisation cycle must be linked.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The unloading of packs after the sterilisation cycle must only occur after verification of sterilisation.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Thirdly, optimising the workflow to improve the reliability of the sterilisation process to reduce the probability of human error.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Fourth, strengthening incident reporting frameworks and ensuring escalation protocols are well understood and adhered to by staff.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And fifth, refining training, competency assessments and regular audits to reinforce staff compliance and understanding of the importance of safety checks that are built into the system, and with full adherence to all processes.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The NHG Review Committee has also recommended new standards for critical steps in the sterilisation process, improved organisation and supervisory management of sterilisation processes, and clarity in incident escalation process.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Some examples include (a) designating a single operator to perform the entire sterilisation process, and (b) ensuring identification of operators of critical steps to enable tracking and traceability in the event of sterilisation failures.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The Ministry will closely monitor the implementation of remedial actions and standards of care at TTSH through follow-up compliance audits, focusing on the area of reprocessing and the sterilisation of instruments.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: These include warnings as well as financial penalties.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We have also asked all healthcare institutions to conduct immediate safety reviews of all their sterilisation processes and to ensure that staff are compliant with the processes.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The Ministry also conducts random ad hoc audits at selected institutions to check on their state of compliance.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This is in addition to the routine inspections of all public and private healthcare institutions which we conduct every two to five years as part of the process of licence renewal.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Healthcare institutions with non-compliances have to rectify them and further inspections are made to verify that such non-compliances have been duly addressed.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: A review of local practices will be undertaken to ensure that they are up-to-date and aligned with the best available evidence for safe sterilisation and disinfection of used instruments.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will then share the learning points across the healthcare system to improve patient safety.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: While we note that the risk of infection to affected patients is extremely low in this incident, it is nonetheless a serious breach of the institution’s infection control system.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Our healthcare institutions need to be more vigilant to enable the detection and mitigation of incidents expeditiously.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In this regard, the Ministry would be working with the healthcare institutions to further enhance the culture of vigilance amongst healthcare professionals so as to promote safe and good quality patient care.
